coverage: Complete defense in both English editions: all named people, identifiable unnamed references, relatives, officials and classical figures; no invented names for generic examples.

entities.name: Socrates
entities.body: The Athenian philosopher defending himself at his trial.

entities.name: Meletus
entities.body: One of Socrates’ three accusers, whom he questions directly in his defense.

entities.name: Anytus
entities.body: One of Socrates’ three accusers, associated with the politicians and craftsmen.

entities.name: Lycon
entities.body: One of Socrates’ three accusers, associated with the public speakers.

entities.name: Aristophanes
entities.body: The Athenian comic playwright whose Clouds caricatures Socrates.

entities.name: Gorgias
entities.body: A traveling teacher of rhetoric from Leontini, charging fees for instruction.

entities.name: Prodicus
entities.body: A traveling teacher from Ceos, charging fees for instruction.

entities.name: Hippias
entities.body: A traveling teacher from Elis, charging fees for instruction.

entities.name: Callias
entities.body: A wealthy Athenian who pays for education from the Sophists. Son of Hipponicus.

entities.name: Hipponicus
entities.body: Callias’ father.

entities.name: Evenus
entities.body: A teacher from Paros whose fees Socrates discusses with Callias.

entities.name: Chaerephon
entities.body: Socrates’ longtime friend, who consulted the oracle at Delphi.

entities.name: The Delphic priestess
entities.body: The priestess who speaks the oracle’s response at Delphi.

entities.name: Chaerephon’s brother
entities.body: The unnamed brother of Chaerephon, present in court.

entities.name: Anaxagoras
entities.body: The philosopher from Clazomenae known for his explanations of the natural world.

entities.name: Euripides
entities.body: The Athenian tragic playwright, mentioned in an editorial note about Anaxagoras.

entities.name: Achilles
entities.body: The Greek warrior at Troy, son of the sea goddess Thetis.

entities.name: Thetis
entities.body: The sea goddess who is Achilles’ mother.

entities.name: Hector
entities.body: The Trojan warrior opposed to Achilles in the Iliad.

entities.name: Patroclus
entities.body: Achilles’ close companion in the Iliad.

entities.name: Zeus
entities.body: The chief god of the Greek pantheon.

entities.name: Leon
entities.body: The man from Salamis whom the Thirty ordered Socrates to arrest.

entities.name: The Thirty
entities.body: The oligarchic rulers who briefly governed Athens after the democracy was overthrown.

entities.name: The Prytanes
entities.body: The presiding members of the Athenian council, among whom Socrates served.

entities.name: The Eleven
entities.body: The Athenian magistrates responsible for prisoners.

entities.name: Crito
entities.body: Socrates’ friend and fellow citizen, father of Critobulus.

entities.name: Critobulus
entities.body: Crito’s son, present at Socrates’ trial.

entities.name: Lysanias
entities.body: Aeschines’ father, from the district of Sphettus.

entities.name: Aeschines
entities.body: An associate of Socrates and son of Lysanias.

entities.name: Antiphon
entities.body: Epigenes’ father, from Cephisus. This is the parent named among Socrates’ supporters.

entities.name: Epigenes
entities.body: An associate of Socrates and son of Antiphon.

entities.name: Nicostratus
entities.body: Theodotus’ brother, named among the relatives supporting Socrates.

entities.name: Theosdotides
entities.body: The father of Nicostratus and Theodotus.

entities.name: Theodotus
entities.body: An associate of Socrates and brother of Nicostratus.

entities.name: Paralus
entities.body: Demodocus’ son and Theages’ brother.

entities.name: Demodocus
entities.body: The father of Paralus and Theages.

entities.name: Theages
entities.body: An associate of Socrates, brother of Paralus and son of Demodocus.

entities.name: Adeimantus
entities.body: Plato’s brother and son of Ariston.

entities.name: Ariston
entities.body: The father of Adeimantus and Plato.

entities.name: Plato
entities.body: Socrates’ associate, present at the trial; also the author of this account.

entities.name: Aeantodorus
entities.body: Apollodorus’ brother, named among Socrates’ supporters.

entities.name: Apollodorus
entities.body: Socrates’ friend and brother of Aeantodorus, present at the trial.

entities.name: Minos
entities.body: The legendary king of Crete, named as a judge of the dead.

entities.name: Rhadamanthus
entities.body: A legendary figure renowned for justice, named as a judge of the dead.

entities.name: Aeacus
entities.body: A legendary Greek king, named as a judge of the dead.

entities.name: Triptolemus
entities.body: The legendary figure associated with teaching agriculture, here named among the judges of the dead.

entities.name: Orpheus
entities.body: The legendary Greek singer and poet.

entities.name: Musaeus
entities.body: A legendary Greek poet associated with sacred song.

entities.name: Hesiod
entities.body: The early Greek poet known for Works and Days and the Theogony.

entities.name: Homer
entities.body: The Greek poet traditionally credited with the Iliad and Odyssey.

entities.name: Palamedes
entities.body: A Greek hero of the Trojan War, cited as a victim of unjust judgment.

entities.name: Ajax
entities.body: The Greek warrior at Troy, son of Telamon.

entities.name: Telamon
entities.body: Ajax’s father in Greek legend.

entities.name: Odysseus
entities.body: The Greek king of Ithaca and hero of the Odyssey.

entities.name: Sisyphus
entities.body: The cunning king of Greek legend, whom Socrates imagines questioning.

entities.name: Agamemnon
entities.body: The commander of the Greek expedition against Troy.
aliases: leader of the great Trojan expedition

entities.name: Socrates’ children
entities.body: Socrates’ three sons, whose upbringing he mentions in his defense. They are not named here.
